sections.overview: It ranges across tropical Asia, reaching Japan, Sulawesi and Kei. Indian records span several states.
sections.identification: Its deep-pink hindwings are shared with T. suffusa, but T. alecto has browner forewings and a pale patch near the hindwing tip.
sections.habitat: The Borneo account describes it as infrequent in lowlands and sometimes collected in cultivated places.
sections.diet: Indian records cite Dillenia, Pisum and Rubia among its larval food plants.
sections.behavior: The species accounts consulted do not describe a distinctive adult activity pattern.
sections.reproduction: The Borneo account describes the caterpillar but gives no detailed account of egg laying or development through the full life cycle.
sections.ecology: It belongs to the same genus as Theretra boisduvalii; see that profile for another regional account of larval hosts.
sections.conservation: The species accounts consulted do not provide a global conservation category or population trend.
